title: AWS Official Practice Exam SAP-C02 — attempt 1 (2026-10-29, scaled 783)

groups.A: Twin options: both look right, the one differing phrase decides
groups.B: Working but wrong fit: the decisive requirement was overlooked (rotation, partial failure, unexpected peak, AZ scope, FIPS level, predictable price)
groups.C: Organizations governance tooling: conformance packs, security account layout, Access Analyzer

9.keywords: rarely accessed after 180 days, must retrieve within 6 hours, MOST cost-effective, Intelligent-Tiering
9.trap: Picked Deep Archive Access tier; its retrieval can take up to 12 hours, breaking the 6-hour SLA. Archive Access restores within minutes to ~5 hours.
9.rule: Intelligent-Tiering: Archive Access (≤ ~5 h) vs Deep Archive Access (≤ 12 h). Match the retrieval SLA first, then pick the cheapest tier that meets it.

11.keywords: Lambda shares RDS credentials, hardcoded, errors on password change, improve security, LEAST development effort
11.trap: Picked Parameter Store + EventBridge-driven custom rotation; Parameter Store has no native RDS rotation, so you build it yourself.
11.rule: DB credentials + rotation with least effort = Secrets Manager managed rotation (single-user/alternating). Parameter Store = config/secrets without built-in rotation.

13.keywords: Organizations, daily EBS backups, CCoE enforce consistently across accounts, MOST reliable
13.trap: Picked a backup policy using Data Lifecycle Manager; Organizations backup policies are an AWS Backup feature, not DLM.
13.rule: Org-wide enforced backups = Organizations backup policy → AWS Backup plans in every account. DLM is per-account EBS/AMI lifecycle.

16.keywords: multi-Region API Gateway, full AND partial failures, reroute automatically, CloudWatch metrics
16.trap: Picked Route 53 Evaluate Target Health; it only sees the endpoint record, not partial failures inside the microservices.
16.rule: Route on application health from many metrics, incl. partial failures = Route 53 Application Recovery Controller routing controls driven by alarms + Lambda.

17.keywords: unexpected peak sales, slow responses, no correlation with time, two EC2 behind ALB
17.trap: Picked scheduled scaling; scheduled actions only fit predictable peaks.
17.rule: Unpredictable load on ALB targets = dynamic target tracking on ALBRequestCountPerTarget. Scheduled scaling only for known calendars.

19.keywords: resilient across multiple AZs, one NAT gateway, DynamoDB tables, increase resilience
19.trap: Picked DynamoDB global tables (multi-Region); DynamoDB is already multi-AZ. The single NAT gateway is the AZ-level single point of failure.
19.rule: Multi-AZ HA review: find the one zonal resource — NAT gateway is per AZ, deploy one per AZ. Don't escalate to multi-Region when the ask is multi-AZ.

21.keywords: tightly coupled HPC, increase network throughput, reduce latency, Select THREE
21.trap: Picked a paravirtual (PV) AMI; PV is legacy and slower. Missed disabling hyperthreading, which helps tightly coupled HPC.
21.rule: Tightly coupled HPC = EFA-capable instances + cluster placement / single AZ + disable hyperthreading (HVM AMIs, never PV).

25.keywords: S3, EBS, EFS, RDS, Volume Gateway, Regional protection, automate, LEAST operational overhead
25.trap: Added RDS cross-Region read replicas on top of AWS Backup; replicas are not backups and add overhead. AWS Backup already covers RDS.
25.rule: One service for S3/EBS/EFS/RDS/Storage Gateway backups with cross-Region copy = AWS Backup plan + vault in another Region.

26.keywords: deploy AWS Config rules to almost all accounts incl. management, exclude a few, prevent unauthorized modification, Select TWO
26.trap: Picked StackSets + drift detection; drift detection only detects changes, it does not prevent them.
26.rule: Org-wide Config rules that member accounts cannot change = organization conformance pack (with excluded accounts) via a delegated admin with trusted access.

30.keywords: runbook describes install and config, LEAST operational overhead, allow future changes
30.trap: Picked CloudFormation for infrastructure but kept the manual runbook steps for software install.
30.rule: Automate the whole runbook: CloudFormation for infra + EC2 user data (or cfn-init) for install/config; change via stack updates.

32.keywords: WorkSpaces, on-prem AD credentials, must not be stored outside the company, SSO to on-prem files
32.trap: Picked AWS Managed Microsoft AD with a trust; that creates a directory (and credentials) in AWS.
32.rule: Use on-prem AD without storing anything in AWS = AD Connector (proxy, no caching). Managed AD = a real directory in AWS.

38.keywords: A/B test two site versions in two S3 buckets, CloudFront, users must not notice
38.trap: Picked path-based behaviors + redirects; different paths and redirects are visible to users.
38.rule: Invisible A/B routing between origins = Lambda@Edge (origin request) choosing the origin by request attributes or cookie.

43.keywords: millions of unencrypted objects, find sensitive data, many apps use the bucket, LEAST development effort
43.trap: Picked copying to a new encrypted bucket; every application would have to change bucket names.
43.rule: Encrypt existing objects in place = default encryption + S3 Inventory + S3 Batch Operations (copy-in-place). Macie finds PII.

45.keywords: Aurora global database, minimize latency, read-after-write consistency, test DR
45.trap: Picked reads from secondary + writes to primary; reads from the secondary may be stale, breaking read-after-write.
45.rule: Aurora Global DB local reads + writes with read-after-write = write forwarding on the secondary; test DR with managed (planned) failover.

53.keywords: eliminate brute-force SSH, log commands per session, keep port forwarding
53.trap: Picked Client VPN; SSH stays open behind the VPN and session commands are not logged.
53.rule: No open SSH + session logs + port forwarding = Systems Manager Session Manager (close port 22, log to S3/CloudWatch).

54.keywords: AWS Batch, custom AMI, restartable jobs, reduce management overhead and cost
54.trap: Picked Fargate Spot; Fargate cannot use a custom AMI.
54.rule: Restartable batch + custom AMI + cheaper = managed EC2 compute environment with Spot. Fargate only when no custom AMI/GPU needs.

57.keywords: 500 workloads, separate accounts, security and infra teams, unique workloads, account structure, Select THREE
57.trap: Picked one centralized security account for logging, tooling and audit; best practice separates them to limit blast radius.
57.rule: Account layout = OUs per environment + SCPs at OU; separate Log Archive, Security Tooling, Audit accounts; Exceptions OU for unique workloads.

58.keywords: grid computing, timeouts between instances, adding instances did not help, LEAST effort
58.trap: Picked enabling ENA; current instances already use ENA. The issue is inter-node latency.
58.rule: Low-latency node-to-node traffic = cluster placement group (relaunch from the AMI).

60.keywords: SQS standard duplicates, instances not scaling, MOST scalable
60.trap: Picked scaling on ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible; queue depth does not change in proportion to fleet size.
60.rule: SQS worker scaling = target tracking on backlog per instance (custom metric: messages ÷ in-service instances). FIFO + dedup removes duplicates.

61.keywords: static files on-prem, apps on multiple servers, NFS directory, one copy, migrate to S3
61.trap: Picked Volume Gateway (iSCSI block); it stores volumes, not S3 objects, and cannot be shared by several servers like NFS.
61.rule: On-prem NFS/SMB access to S3 objects = S3 File Gateway. Volume Gateway = iSCSI block volumes; Tape Gateway = VTL.

62.keywords: SQS queue shared across org accounts, identify external principals with access
62.trap: Picked CloudTrail data events; logs only show who called the API, not who is allowed by the policy.
62.rule: Who outside the org CAN access a resource = IAM Access Analyzer with the organization as zone of trust (external access findings).

64.keywords: 50 accounts, SSH only from trusted CIDRs, compliant, cannot be modified by accounts, Firewall Manager
64.trap: Picked a stateful strict-order group with the allow rule given the highest order number; the deny 0.0.0.0/0 rule is evaluated first and blocks trusted SSH too.
64.rule: Firewall Manager + Network Firewall: rules evaluate from the lowest priority number — put the trusted-CIDR allow first, deny-all after.

65.keywords: HR and Recruiting share SCP requirements, Recruiting stricter, avoid duplicate effort, LEAST effort
65.trap: Picked removing accounts from the organization and re-inviting them — far more effort than moving accounts between OUs.
65.rule: Shared + extra restrictions = nest the stricter OU under the shared one (SCPs inherit); move accounts between OUs, never out of the org.

66.keywords: projected EC2 costs, notify CFO, stop instances, LOWEST risk of overspending
66.trap: Picked sending the alert to an operator to stop instances manually; human delay leaves the overspend risk.
66.rule: Budgets alert on forecasted cost + Budgets action (stop EC2/RDS, apply IAM/SCP) = automatic guardrail.

68.keywords: DynamoDB on-demand, bursts, few hot keys repeatedly read, reduce cost, LEAST overhead
68.trap: Picked DAX + Savings Plans; Savings Plans do not cover DynamoDB.
68.rule: Hot keys → DAX; predictable load → provisioned capacity + auto scaling (or reserved capacity). Savings Plans = EC2/Fargate/Lambda/SageMaker only.

70.keywords: FIPS 140-2 Level 3, keys available only business hours, highly available, MOST cost-effective
70.trap: Picked KMS with scheduled disable/enable; the exam treats KMS as Level 2. (Real AWS: KMS HSMs gained Level 3 validation in 2023.)
70.rule: Exam rule: FIPS 140-2 Level 3 / dedicated HSM = CloudHSM (multi-AZ cluster). Cost trick: delete/restore the cluster from backup outside hours.

73.keywords: PHP LAMP developer, little AWS expertise, stable traffic, predictable pricing, least time to learn
73.trap: Picked Elastic Beanstalk + DynamoDB; pay-per-resource pricing and a new NoSQL database both break the asks.
73.rule: Simple LAMP app + fixed monthly price + minimal AWS learning = Amazon Lightsail.

74.keywords: existing bucket default settings, no delete or overwrite for 5 years, Object Lock compliance mode
74.trap: Picked enabling Object Lock on the existing bucket; the exam key assumes Object Lock only on new buckets. (Real AWS: Object Lock can be enabled on existing versioned buckets since late 2023.)
74.rule: WORM for N years = Versioning + Object Lock compliance mode with default retention. Exam key: create a new bucket and move objects.
